description: Agent-consumable source registry for social and cultural event discovery. The current catalog targets NYC, but each source independently declares its location, retrieval method, authentication needs, and parser expectations.

dedup.note: Use URL+time only for a specific event page. Calendar/index URLs represent many events and must fall back to venue+time+title. Never key on title alone.

fetch_policy.source_contract: Each sources[].retrieval_profile selects an ordered recipe from retrieval_profiles.
fetch_policy.fallback_rule: Use a fallback only when the primary fails or returns an unverified zero. Record the actual method and recipe version in social.db.
fetch_policy.zero_rule: Zero is valid only when the profile's explicit empty signal is observed; otherwise record empty_suspicious and audit.

source_activation.disabled_rule: A source with enabled=false remains in the catalog but is excluded from plans and manifests. disabled_reason is required and must state what would justify re-enabling it.

run_config.preferences_note: Personal fit and ranking criteria are NOT defined here. They live in the local EVENT_RANKING_CRITERIA.md file and apply only after retrieval, factual validation, and deduplication. This registry defines where and how to retrieve events. It never uses personal fit to reject a factual candidate.

extraction_pipeline.note: Do not accumulate raw page text in context. Store large evidence in .cache and operational results in social.db.
steps: Create a database-backed run for every enabled source selected for this crawl.
Retrieve each source with its declared primary recipe, using fallbacks only when required.
Write large raw responses and screenshots under .cache and retain their paths and hashes.
Record each source result and every candidate in social.db before finalization.
Finalize the run so candidates are validated, deduplicated, and added to the event store.
extraction_pipeline.runtime_note: Runtime does not matter — this runs in the background. Prefer completeness over speed.

run_config.etiquette: Most of these are small independent venues and nonprofits. Don't hammer them, don't spoof a user agent, don't evade bot detection. If a site is actively blocking automation, that's an answer — move it to manual_check rather than working around it.

luma-calendar-api-v1.empty_signal: Successful API response with an empty entries collection.
luma-calendar-api-v1.note: Resolve calendar_api_id, then call api.lu.ma/calendar/get-items with period=future.

eventbrite-organizer-v1.empty_signal: Organizer page explicitly reports no upcoming events.

meetup-group-v1.empty_signal: Group page explicitly reports zero upcoming events.

http-calendar-v1.empty_signal: Calendar explicitly reports no upcoming events.

browser-calendar-v1.empty_signal: Rendered calendar explicitly reports no upcoming events.

browser-directory-v1.empty_signal: None: a known directory returning zero outbound targets is suspicious.

authenticated-browser-v1.empty_signal: Authenticated event or invitation view explicitly reports no upcoming items.

partiful-calendar-v1.empty_signal: Calendar import succeeds and contains no Partiful events in the window.

directory-http-v1.empty_signal: None: a known directory returning zero outbound targets is suspicious.

link-hub-v1.empty_signal: None: zero outbound links is always suspicious.

daily-html-listing-v1.empty_signal: A current dated post exists and contains no dated event records in the configured window.

luma-category-api-v1.empty_signal: A terminal, chronologically ordered public discovery response has no NYC events in the requested date window.
luma-category-api-v1.note: Use the public Luma discovery category endpoint with NYC coordinates, strict local date filtering, and cursor pagination.

sources.title: 57 — calendar
sources.parse_hint: The gather_community_calendar Python adapter reads the anonymous structured feed used by the public 57 community calendar. It paginates event entities for the requested date window, stores only sanitized event facts, and never retains member, profile, or reaction data or raw API responses. Community-submitted third-party and non-NYC events are valid candidates; normal deduplication and the later fit-ranking phase handle overlap, geography, access restrictions, and fit. Keep the browser calendar profile as the independent visible-page audit and fallback path.

sources.title: Metrograph
sources.parse_hint: Dedicated special-events page. The metrograph_special_events Python adapter reads only the special-event cards and does not emit ordinary showtimes. It preserves each dated showtime and direct ticket URL. A present but empty special-events section is the verified empty signal. Keep the HTTP calendar profile as the independent audit and fallback path.

sources.title: Anthology Film Archives — Calendar
sources.parse_hint: Official public Veezi sessions page for Anthology Film Archives. The anthology_veezi_jsonld Python adapter makes one request to this page, reads VisualArtsEvent JSON-LD, and emits one event per ticket session. It never requests purchase URLs. A zero is verified only when the page has an explicit no-sessions signal or the complete session list covers the requested end date. Anthology RSS can audit title and date counts, but it lacks complete time data. Do not fetch the Anthology calendar route because its robots rules disallow it.

sources.title: Analog Film NYC — Upcoming screenings
sources.parse_hint: Citywide aggregate of celluloid screenings. The analog_film_nyc Python adapter makes one request to the official page, parses explicit dated day sections, and emits only ticketed screenings with a stated time. It keeps multi-film programs as one occurrence, uses the listed venue as host, and does not fetch outbound ticket pages. A ticketed item without an explicit time is rejected instead of inferred. A zero is verified only when dated sections cover every day in the requested window. Expect heavy overlap with Metrograph, Anthology, and Nitehawk; deduplicate normally.

sources.disabled_reason: Disabled because this is a cinema directory with no dated programming. Re-enable if it publishes a complete dated calendar or the crawler gains a separate venue-discovery workflow.

sources.title: Nitehawk Cinema
sources.parse_hint: Dine-in cinema. The nitehawk Python adapter reads both venue coming-soon pages and the Prospect Park movie-trivia schedule. sources.title: Brooklyn Museum — First Saturdays
sources.parse_hint: First Saturdays subset of the Brooklyn Museum public program API. The brooklyn_museum_search Python adapter uses the exact First Saturdays subtype, validates it locally, and paginates an explicit date window. sources.title: Brooklyn Museum — All programs
sources.parse_hint: Broad Brooklyn Museum program feed. The brooklyn_museum_search Python adapter queries the public search API with an explicit date window, start date order, and pagination. sources.title: Casa Italiana Zerilli-Marimò (NYU) — Events

Primary path: the casa_italiana Python adapter queries the official same-origin WordPress Events Calendar API with an explicit date window and pagination. sources.title: Istituto Italiano di Cultura New York — Events

The iic_new_york_events Python adapter sends an explicit date window, paginates the listing, and fetches only matching details for time, place, fee, status, and description. An explicit no-results message is the verified empty signal. Keep the HTTP calendar profile as the independent audit and fallback path.

sources.title: L'Alliance New York (formerly FIAF) — Calendar
sources.parse_hint: Current official L'Alliance New York event archive; the legacy events.fiaf.org calendar is stale. The lalliance_events Python adapter makes one request to the server-rendered archive and emits only explicit dated and timed occurrences. It does not paginate, fetch details, or use the incomplete WordPress REST data. Date-only cards are retained as missing_explicit_time rejections instead of receiving an invented time. Past-tagged cards are rejected. A structurally valid future-only archive can verify an empty window. Keep the HTTP calendar profile as the independent audit and fallback path.

sources.title: Out There — Straight NYC Singles Events
sources.parse_hint: Primary execution path: the out_there Python adapter. It uses HTTP only. Keep orientation=straight on every paginated request and follow page=N until there is no Next page. Listing pages return 24 event URLs in ItemList JSON-LD. Detail pages provide Event JSON-LD; the adapter also reads the small header tag area for factual age limits. Preserve the Out There event URL, direct signup URL, organizer, description, availability, precise venue, and factual age limits. Treat an explicit zero total or a verified zero inside the configured date window as empty. Expect overlap with organizer and Eventbrite sources; deduplicate normally. The browser calendar recipe remains the independent audit and fallback path.

manual_check.description: Instagram-only sources. Deliberately excluded from automated runs: Instagram walls content behind login, actively detects automation, and buries event details in captions and expiring Stories. Repeated automated access risks rate-limiting or flagging the operator's personal account for low structured yield. Check these by hand when useful.

run_contract.description: Data that each run must retain for inspection in the web control center.
constraints: Read-only. Never RSVP, purchase, join, or submit a form on the operator's behalf.
Never enter payment details or credentials.
Retain an explicit rejection for candidates that cannot be ingested for a factual or validation reason. Never use personal ranking criteria as a retrieval rejection reason.
Log every source that returned zero results, distinguishing 'no events in window' from 'fetch failed' from 'auth required'.
Never omit a source from the per-source accounting records.

per_source_accounting.note: MANDATORY. The operator uses this as the feedback loop on which sources are worth keeping. Every source attempted must appear with an explicit count and state. A source that is silently absent is indistinguishable from one that returned nothing, which destroys the signal.
per_source_accounting.emit_row_for: every enabled source selected for this run, including ones that failed or returned nothing

states.ok: Fetched and parsed successfully. events_kept means accepted for ingestion before fit ranking. Report events_found and events_kept even when both are 0.
states.ok_via_fallback: Primary recipe failed or returned an unverified zero; a fallback succeeded and validated.
states.empty_verified: Recipe succeeded and its explicit empty signal was observed.
states.empty_suspicious: Extraction returned zero without its explicit empty signal. Run a fallback and audit.
states.parse_failed: Fetched content but extracted nothing — the site likely changed structure. REPORT LOUDLY; this is the failure that hides itself.
states.validation_failed: Candidates were parsed but required fields were missing or implausible.
states.fetch_failed: Network/HTTP error. Include the error. Retry once before reporting.
states.auth_required: Session expired or absent. Do not retry-loop against a login form.
states.blocked: Structurally unreachable in this environment, e.g. the Gmail-dependent inbox sources.

also_retain: Total candidates across all sources, before and after deduplication.
Source state changes since the previous run.
New hosts seen repeatedly that are not yet in this registry.

run_contract.ranking_note: After retrieval, factual validation, and deduplication, rank each event against the local EVENT_RANKING_CRITERIA.md file. Ranking is not a computed score. There is deliberately no boost_score field because the criteria are prose and can change. A fit decision never changes retrieval results or ingestion counts.
